sentences.text: The ocean is salty, and rivers aren't. So where did all that salt come from?
Rainwater is slightly acidic, so it slowly erodes rocks on land and frees up dissolved minerals.
Streams and rivers carry those minerals to the sea. Living things use some of them, but others stay, so their concentration builds up over time.
Rivers taste fresh because rain keeps refilling them. The ocean collects everything that flows in.
Openings in the seafloor, called hydrothermal vents, add salts too.
By one estimate, the salt in the ocean, spread evenly over all land, would make a layer more than five hundred feet thick.
So, if rivers keep delivering salt for ages... is the ocean just the planet's most patient collector, or its saltiest hoarder?
